title: Wittmann leads a BMW one-two-three-four to regain the lead
dek: Marco Wittmann won Race 2 from pole by 4.123s from Tom Blomqvist in a BMW one-two-three-four and retook the championship lead from Robert Wickens, who finished fifth with failing steering.

chapters.title: Wet Saturday to Mercedes, dry Sunday to answer
text: Saturday had belonged to Mercedes. Wickens won the rain-affected Race 1 from second on the grid, the Mercedes cars filled the first four places, and Wittmann finished 19th and gave up the championship lead. Wickens went into Sunday on 108 points, Wittmann was on 105, Green on 104, and Mortara and di Resta were level on 92.

Several BMW drivers had said after the wet race that they expected to be stronger on a dry track, and Sunday brought exactly that. The second race of the weekend was set for an hour, and Wittmann's reply began in qualifying.

chapters.title: Wittmann takes pole as Martin crashes
text: On a dry circuit the BMW drivers took the front of the grid. Wittmann was fastest on 1:28.776, with Tom Blomqvist 0.102s behind on 1:28.878. The session was briefly interrupted when Maxime Martin, who had been fastest at the time, lost control of his BMW in a quick left-hander and slid into the tyre barrier. He was unhurt, and his mechanics had the car repaired in time for the race, but he lost his grid position and had to start from the back of the field.

Martin's removal promoted Wickens to third on the grid, with Bruno Spengler fourth, Daniel Juncadella fifth and Augusto Farfus sixth. Timo Glock was seventh, Maximilian Götz eighth, Lucas Auer ninth and António Félix da Costa tenth.

It was a poor session for Audi, which had no car in the top ten. Nico Müller was the best of them in 12th, Mattias Ekström 14th, Mortara 17th and Green 19th. Gary Paffett, the previous day's pole-sitter, was 21st, and di Resta started 11th.

chapters.title: Wittmann pulls clear while Blomqvist holds off Wickens
text: Wittmann led from the start and was never challenged. Wickens, who had inherited third on the grid, ran behind Blomqvist, and the BMW driver concentrated on keeping the Mercedes behind him while Wittmann built a lead.

The pit stops changed little at the front. Blomqvist kept second place, and the gap between the two BMWs settled in the region of four seconds for the rest of the race. Spengler, who had been struggling for grip early on, was left out longer than most by his team, and he rejoined between Wickens and Juncadella.

chapters.title: Failing steering costs Wickens the podium
text: Wickens had been running third, but his car developed steering trouble. He said it became progressively heavier and then stopped working altogether, and he later damaged the front of the car in contact with Martin Tomczyk after his stop. Spengler passed the Mercedes in the second half of the race and went on to take third place.
Wickens had a queue of cars behind him, with Juncadella the first of them. Farfus nevertheless got past both Mercedes to take fourth, but Wickens nursed the damaged car home in fifth.

chapters.title: Contacts and drive-throughs wreck the title rivals' afternoons
text: Mortara made the most of the afternoon. He started 17th and drove his way up to sixth, and he and Wickens crossed the line side by side, the Mercedes finishing 0.067s ahead. Nico Müller took seventh and the fastest lap of the race, a 1:30.269 on lap 25.

Two of the championship contenders lost their points to the stewards. Green climbed quickly from 19th, but collided with da Costa and was given a drive-through penalty, and he was given a second one for speeding in the pit lane while serving it, finishing 22nd. Di Resta lunged at Glock late in the race, hit the BMW and sent it into the gravel, where it was out of the race, and received a drive-through penalty of his own. He finished 20th.
Martin recovered from the back of the grid to 17th, in spite of a drive-through penalty.

chapters.title: BMW fills the first four places
text: Wittmann took the chequered flag after 40 laps and 1:02:03.216, 4.123s ahead of Blomqvist. Spengler was third, 18.119s behind the winner, and Farfus fourth at 24.650s, which gave BMW the first four places. It was Wittmann's second win of the season and the seventh of his DTM career, in his 50th race.

Wickens was fifth, 38.818s behind, with Mortara 0.067s further back in sixth. Müller, Adrien Tambay, Ekström and Auer completed the top ten, Auer's tenth place being the second-best Mercedes result of the day.

chapters.title: Wittmann back on top, Wickens and Audi's rivals hurt
text: The result put Wittmann back at the head of the championship on 130 points, 12 ahead of Wickens on 118. Green stayed on 104, Mortara moved to 100 and di Resta remained on 92. Wittmann had finished 19th on Saturday, and he said afterwards that the team had simply written that race off. He dedicated the win to his race engineer, who celebrated a birthday that day.

BMW's motorsport director Jens Marquardt called the result remarkable after Saturday's race and said some rivals had shown unfair manoeuvres that the championship did not need. Glock, who had been running in the points when he was hit, finished the weekend without a point. Di Resta described the contact as a 50:50 situation in which Glock had left the door open and then closed it again, and he said his race was over after that. Glock said the blow came from di Resta, and BMW's team principal called his retirement unnecessary.

For Mercedes it was a bittersweet day. Wickens said the steering failure meant he could scarcely believe he had reached the finish. Audi's motorsport chief Wolfgang Ullrich said the weekend had not gone as planned, and that it was not yet understood what had gone wrong in qualifying, though four Audis still scored. Mortara described his climb from 17th to sixth as one of the biggest recoveries of his DTM career, and Green, who admitted he had been too optimistic in trying to pass da Costa, said six races remained and that he would not give up.

BMW led the manufacturers' standings with 436 points, ahead of Audi on 390 and Mercedes on 386, and Marquardt said BMW now led all three championships. Six races remained, starting at the Nürburgring on 10 and 11 September.

facts.v: Wittmann, Blomqvist, Spengler and Farfus filled the first four places, with Wittmann leading from pole.

one.label: AUTO BILD: Wittmann siegt in Moskau

facts.v: Martin was fastest in qualifying when he slid into the tyre barrier, lost his grid slot and started from the back, finishing 17th.
Green was penalised for hitting da Costa and then again for speeding in the pit lane while serving the first penalty.
Wittmann moved to 130 points, 12 ahead of Wickens, after starting the day three points behind.

one.label: SPORT1: Marco Wittmann und BMW triumphieren

facts.v: Wickens lost his power steering and still held on to fifth place, 0.067s ahead of Mortara.
